title: Private Deploy: Zero‑Egress Tunnel Profiles and Operator Quiesce PRD
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem statement: Customers who require fully isolated VPC/private deployments (no general outbound internet egress) need a predictable, auditable upgrade and operator lifecycle. Current upgrade flows assume transient egress for image fetches or telemetry. This PRD defines a set of minimal 'zero-egress tunnel profiles' plus an operator quiesce protocol and acceptance criteria so upgrades, emergency patches, and operator actions can be performed without violating air‑gap constraints. Goals: 1) Define network policies/operators that require zero sustained outbound connectivity, 2) Provide a documented short-lived egress tunnel mode for tightly controlled maintenance windows, 3) Define operator quiesce API and deterministic rollback criteria, 4) Ensure observability and auditability without persistent egress.
background: Large enterprise and regulated customers run Redwood Private with strict outbound controls; they require deterministic upgrade behavior and explicit approvals for any egress.
Recent incidents (private customer upgrade failures) highlighted flaky image fetches when outbound proxies were briefly unavailable, causing prolonged rollbacks.

Existing acceptance criteria focus on offline mirroring and operatorless bootstraps; there is a gap for controlled ephemeral egress modes and operator quiesce semantics needed during maintenance and emergency patching.
scope: Define and implement three tunnel profiles: 'none' (strict zero egress), 'ephemeral-proxy' (timeboxed tunnel with signed token), 'mirror-fetch' (operator-triggered pull via verified mirror).
Add an Operator Quiesce API to pause workstreams, drain in-flight tokens, snapshot KV caches, and mark nodes as maintenance for safe upgrades/patches.
Acceptance tests, canary flow and rollback policy for upgrades under each profile.
Audit logs and telemetry stubs that are allowed under zero-egress (local-only) and a design for optional signed telemetry transfer when approved.
out_of_scope: Implementing third-party commercial proxies or customer-specific manifest signing workflows (we will provide hooks and documentation).
Built-in data exfiltration prevention beyond network controls (customers are expected to enforce host/network-level controls).
requirements: REQ-1: Tunnel Profiles - system must support 'none', 'ephemeral-proxy', and 'mirror-fetch' as first-class config fields on cluster and operator rollout manifests.
REQ-2: Ephemeral Tunnel Authorization - ephemeral-proxy must accept a signed timebound JWT issued by customer KMS/HSM; operator actions using this tunnel must be auditable and reversible.
REQ-3: Operator Quiesce API - POST /operator/quiesce with params {duration_minutes, reason, allowed_actions} that atomically signals nodes to drain new requests and persist KV cache state.

REQ-4: Deterministic Rollback - every upgrade initiated under a tunnel profile must embed a deterministic rollback checkpoint (image checksum + KV snapshot ID) and automated rollback triggers for upgrade-age > X minutes or health regressions.

REQ-5: Canary Simulation - ability to simulate partitioned canary where a single private site runs the upgrade path without any egress and validates KV replay and model artifact integrity from a local mirror.

REQ-6: Audit and Telemetry - all tunnel activations, operator quiesce events, approval tokens, and image checksums must be stored in local audit logs and optionally exported when a signed transfer is executed by customer; Redwood must not initiate unsanctioned outbound flows.
REQ-7: UX/Operator Feedback - Console must surface current tunnel profile, time remaining for ephemeral tunnels, and escalation playbooks when quiesce is active.
REQ-8: Timeboxed Failure Modes - if ephemeral tunnel fails mid-upgrade, system must enter a safe-fail state, stop the upgrade, and surface rollback instructions to operator.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Zero-egress baseline - A freshly provisioned private cluster configured with tunnel profile='none' successfully completes a dry-run upgrade simulation that validates image digests against local mirror and returns PASS without any outbound network attempts (verified via packet captures).

AC-2: Ephemeral-proxy flow - Customer operator can request an ephemeral tunnel with a signed JWT; Redwood accepts the token, performs exactly the approved actions during the timeframe, writes an immutable audit entry, and closes the tunnel at expiration. Test: initiate a patch under ephemeral-proxy, token expires mid-patch, system halts and rolls back to checkpoint automatically.

AC-3: Mirror-fetch validation - Upgrades using 'mirror-fetch' succeed when images and model artifacts are present on local mirror; if mirror lacks artifact, the operator receives deterministic error and guidance; no fallback to public egress is attempted.

AC-4: Operator quiesce correctness - Quiesce API pauses new request ingress, drains in-flight generation sessions within configured timeout, persists KV cache snapshot, and annotations appear in audit logs with operator identity and reason. Recovery path must resume normal traffic and validate KV integrity after restart.

AC-5: Canary and rollback - Canary run on one private site completes tests; if health regressions detected during canary or in manual failover, automated rollback to the checkpoint is executed in < 5 minutes and logs retained.

AC-6: Telemetry export policy - No telemetry leaves the cluster unless a signed transfer is initiated; when initiated, data package contains the cryptographic signature and an audit trail of the approval. Verification test must show package validated by customer's public key.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Dev + internal): Implement tunnel profile primitives and Quiesce API; run lab upgrades in air-gapped testbeds (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (Alpha customers): Pilot with 2 existing private customers willing to run canary with operator oversight; collect feedback and iterate (4 weeks).
Phase 3 (General availability): Document runbooks and add Console UI exposures; release private-2026.04 with compatibility notes and operator training (2 weeks).
Emergency patch path: Provide an operator checklist and signed-token template for live emergency patches; require 2-step approval from customer admin and Redwood SE.
test_scenarios: TS-1: Packet-capture verification during 'none' profile dry-run upgrade (no outbound SYN observed).
TS-2: Token expiry mid-upgrade triggers safe-fail and rollback to checkpoint; verify rollback completes and service returns to prior SLO.
TS-3: Mirror-missing artifact path produces deterministic failure code and suggested remediation steps without attempting egress.
TS-4: Quiesce + restart: trigger quiesce, simulate node crash during quiesce, restart operator, validate KV snapshot recovery and reconcile without data loss.
TS-5: Audit integrity: export signed audit bundle from cluster and validate signature and provenance with customer public key.
monitoring_and_observability: Emit events: TUNNEL_ACTIVATED, TUNNEL_EXPIRED, QUIESCE_STARTED, QUIESCE_COMPLETED, UPGRADE_CHECKPOINT_CREATED, UPGRADE_ROLLBACK_EXECUTED.
Console: show tunnel profile, expiry timer, active quiesce owner, current checkpoint ID, and last export bundle hash.
Retention: Local audit logs retained 90 days by default; exported bundles tracked in S3-like mirrors by customer.
open_questions: Q1: Should Redwood provide an optional signed token issuer as a managed service for customers without KMS? (security implications).
Q2: What is the maximum allowed ephemeral tunnel duration by policy? Proposed default: 60 minutes, adjustable by customer off-band approval.
Q3: Do we need a mechanism to throttle operator-triggered mirror fetches to prevent resource exhaustion? (rate limiting on mirror pulls).
notes: This PRD intentionally focuses on deterministic behaviors and operator primitives; implementation should avoid any heuristics that attempt silent egress fallbacks.
Design must be compatible with existing mirror bootstrap mechanisms (no breaking changes).
